lists.of: questions about possible causes of illusions
items: 61. Could the illusion of reliability of intuition : be caused by : reliance on a single system?
62. Could the illusion of reliability of mass opinion : be caused by : monodeism (excessive preoccupation with a single, fixed idea)?
63. Could the illusion of reliability or orthodoxy : be caused by : persistence despite (or actually via) transformation (meta-continuity)?
64. Could the illusion of reliability of 'proofs' : be caused by : reification or hypostatization?
65. Could the illusion of reliability of the senses : be caused by : reification or hypostatization?
66. Could the illusion of resources finite : be caused by : neuropsychological heredity: e.g., inherited modes, gestalten, or elements of perception, thought, feeling, or action?
67. Could the illusion of resources infinite : be caused by : false gestalten or syntheses?
68. Could the illusion of rising or setting of sun, moon, or stars : be caused by : imperfections or costs of common sense?
69. Could the illusion of science mostly complete : be caused by : erroneous substitution of part for whole?
70. Could the illusion of scientific mechanism (mechanomorphic cosmos) : be caused by : static or dynamic configurations?
71. Could the illusion of self-sufficiency of the individual : be caused by : wanton desire?
72. Could the illusion of separability of form and content : be caused by : simplism?
73. Could the illusion of simultaneity : be caused by : false or inadequate world view?
74. Could the illusion of single answers to questions : be caused by : deficiencies of fundamental knowledge: e.g., imprecise or undefined mathematics, geometry, physics, ethics, etc?
75. Could the illusion of single causes : be caused by : static or dynamic configurations?
76. Could the illusion of smooth surfaces (e.g., absolute smoothness of a metal surface) : be caused by : ignorance (lack of information)?
77. Could the illusion of solar constancy : be caused by : misconstrual of function from appearance or mis-supposition of appearance from function?
78. Could the illusion of solid matter : be caused by : perceptual or mental expedience?
79. Could the illusion of space independent of time : be caused by : personification or self-projection?
80. Could the illusion of stability of civilization : be caused by : misdescription, under-description, or under-perception?
81. Could the illusion of stable, static universe : be caused by : insufficient criteria of illusioniness?
82. Could the illusion of stereotypes : be caused by : continuity?
83. Could the illusion of 'superficiality' of reality : be caused by : misinformation?
84. Could the illusion of superiority or uniqueness of one's culture : be caused by : cooperative phenomena or interdependences?
85. Could the illusion of that energy is lost : be caused by : homology of perceptual categories?
86. Could the illusion of that what we know is known to us : be caused by : paninterpretansformability?
87. Could the illusion of the present (its thinness or absolute separation from past or future) : be caused by : "mental excuses"?
88. Could the illusion of transcendence of history : be caused by : arbitrary decisions?
89. Could the illusion of unambiguous statements : be caused by : deception or fraud?
90. Could the illusion of unbiased thought : be caused by : excessive abstraction, theoretical fictions, or neglect of concrete facts?
91. Could the illusion of understanding of one's real motives : be caused by : simplism?
92. Could the illusion of unique things : be caused by : perspective (e.g., limited, fixed, specialized, or local) or by defective coordinate systems or coordinates?
93. Could the illusion of uniqueness of the present : be caused by : expectation?
94. Could the illusion of validity of habits : be caused by : 'Pan-Truth' (misapplication of the doctrine so-named) or pan-paradox?
95. Could the illusion of word-thing or concept-thing identity : be caused by : reliance on a single system?
96. Could the illusion of omnipercipience (all-visibility of nature) : be caused by : mis-remembrance or paramnesia?

notes: The title and preceding portion of the list are outside the photograph; a cropped fragment above item 61 was omitted.
